articleBody:
- [ ] Measure total wall width and depth — Ensures your new vanity cabinet will not block doorways, shower entries, or toilet clearance.
- [ ] Record water shutoff valve and drain heights — Confirms existing rough-in plumbing fits inside the cabinet without cutting into interior drawers or shelves.
- [ ] Check electrical outlet distance from the basin — Verifies your setup supports required GFCI receptacles placed within 3 feet of the sink edge.
- [ ] Measure mirror and light fixture clearance — Prevents taller vanity tops or backsplashes from colliding with wall sconces or hanging medicine cabinets.
- [ ] Confirm floor tile coverage beneath old cabinet — Identifies whether bare subfloor will show if switching to a floating vanity or a narrower footprint.
- [ ] Inspect wall drywall and baseboards for water stains — Catches hidden moisture damage behind the existing sink before mounting new cabinetry.
- [ ] Verify wall stud locations along mounting line — Ensures heavy solid-wood cabinets or wall-mounted floating vanities anchor directly into solid framing.
- [ ] Check drawer and door opening radiuses — Prevents vanity drawers from hitting the bathroom entry door, heat registers, or toilet rim.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through each item with a tape measure before ordering your vanity package.
